headline: Approved solar power deals for Tenney and CGS schools, declared Pleasant Valley and Currier school properties surplus for housing, tabled a trash-fee ordinance.
summary: The Council approved fire department promotions, a new Veterans Service Officer, solar panel power-purchase agreements for the Tenney and Comprehensive Grammar Schools, and resolutions declaring the Pleasant Valley School, Currier School, and 30 Railroad Street properties surplus for future sale and housing redevelopment. It tabled a National Grid utility grant and an ordinance overhauling trash cart fees and fines, while approving a lien ordinance for unpaid trash fees and new ambulance/lift-assist fees.
decisions: Appointed Lieutenant Michael Ferris to Deputy Chief, approved unanimously.
Promoted Firefighter Eric Moreau to Lieutenant, approved unanimously.
Appointed Jordan Normandia as Veterans Service Officer, approved unanimously.
Approved the minutes of the Special Meeting May 26, 2026 FY'2027 Municipal Budget, Second Read, unanimously.
Approved the minutes of the June 8, 2026 Regular Meeting, 8 yes, 1 present.
Moved the citation for Victor Rivera, Jr. to the August 3, 2026 agenda.
Tabled Public Service Grant 301043582 for Temple Drive, Westgate Circle, and Jewel Circle (National Grid conduit project), 6-2.
Approved the Solar Project License Agreement with Solect Energy for Tenney Grammar School, 75 Pleasant Street, 6-2.
Approved the Solar Project License Agreement with Solect Energy for Comprehensive Grammar School, 100 Howe Street, 6-2.
Approved contract C-27-1 with Brox Industries, Inc. for paving materials in the amount of $111,425.00, unanimously.
Approved contract C-27-2 with Kitchen and Floor Décor, Inc. for Marsh Grammar School carpet removal and tile installation, $83,375.00, unanimously.
Approved contract C-27-3 with Valerio, Dominello & Hillman, LLC for legal services, Fiscal Year 2027, $5,000.00, unanimously.
Approved contract C-27-4, a Power Purchase Agreement with Solect Energy for Tenney Grammar School, 7-1.
Approved contract C-27-5, a Power Purchase Agreement with Solect Energy for Comprehensive Grammar School, 7-1.
Accepted Cooper Lane as a public way (TR-25-75), unanimously.
Approved resolution TR-26-53 requesting an insurance review and competitive quotes for city insurance coverage, unanimously.
Approved ordinance TO-26-12 to rezone a parcel fronting Arcadia Street for commercial improvement, unanimously.
Tabled ordinance TO-26-16, amending trash and recyclables collection fees and fines, unanimously.
Approved ordinance TO-26-17 amending the municipal charges lien section to allow liens for trash fines, unanimously.
Failed a motion to set a minimum sale price of $125,000 for the Pleasant Valley School property, 2-6.
Approved resolution TR-26-67 declaring the Pleasant Valley School property, 180 Pleasant Valley Street, surplus for sale and redevelopment, as amended, unanimously.
Approved resolution TR-26-68 declaring the Currier School property, 36 Boylston Street, surplus for sale and redevelopment, unanimously.
Approved resolution TR-26-69 accepting a $15,795.31 Fiscal Year 2027 State 911 Emergency Medical Dispatch grant, unanimously.
Approved resolution TR-26-70 accepting a $168,186.09 Fiscal Year 2027 State 911 Department Training Grant, unanimously.
Approved resolution TR-26-71 authorizing a transfer between FY26 General Fund budgets, unanimously.
Approved resolution TR-26-73 declaring the property at 30 Railroad Street surplus for sale and redevelopment, unanimously.
Approved resolution TR-26-74 transferring funds from the Edwin J. Castle Fund to the Methuen Literacy Project and Methuen Public Schools CTE Early Childhood Care, unanimously.
Approved ordinance TO-26-18 increasing ambulance rates and establishing a new lift assist fee, unanimously.

METHUEN CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES                                        
Monday, JULY 6th, 2026 @ 6:00 P.M.   
METHUEN HIGH SCHOOL MEDIA CENTER, Ranger Road 
 
1. Roll Call - all members present – Clr. Santos, Clr. Simard, Clr. Valley, Clr. 
DiZoglio, Clr. Drew, Clr. MacLaren, Clr. Marsan, Clr. Pesce and Chair Soto 
 
2. Acceptance of the Agenda – Motion to accept the agenda by Clr. Drew, seconded by 
Clr. Santos – Motion to move Consideration of Appointments after Public 
Participation by Clr. Santos, seconded by Clr. DiZoglio – UPON ROLL CALL 
VOTE – 8 yes, 1 no (Clr. Drew) – Motion to approve the agenda as amended by Clr. 
Marsan, seconded by Clr. DiZoglio – UPON ROLL CALL VOTE – unanimously

3. Pledge of Allegiance/Moment of Silence – Chair Soto recognized Clr. DiZoglio for a 
Moment of Silence for Jim Dawe, “Since 2018, Jim faithfully covered the majority of the 
City Council meetings as part of the Methuen Community Studios family. Every other 
Monday night residents could count on Jim being here, helping ensure that local 
government remained accessible to the community. Those who worked alongside him 
knew that Jim could never start a meeting without his McDonald's in hand. Jim was also 
an important part of the MCS production team and was always on scene in the MCS 
van covering parades, Methuen High School sports, and countless other community 
events. Beyond his work with Methuen Community Studios, Jim was also known 
throughout the community for decades of service as president of Methuen Little League. 
He made an immeasurable impact on generations of Methuen families, coaching and 
monitoring countless young people over the years. Through baseball, Jim taught not 
only the game itself but also teamwork, sportsmanship, and community spirit. Jim's 
dedication, dependability, and quiet presence will be missed by all who knew him.” 
 
4. Public Participation  
• Joseph McDonald, 40 Swan Avenue, Methuen - Good evening. My name is Joseph 
McDonald and I live at 40 Swan Avenue in Methuen, Mass. And today I am here to 
speak about the MEVA bus strike that is happening. The streets of Methuen and the 
streets across the Merrimack Valley feel different right now. They seem more crowded. 
They seem more stressed. And for thousands of us in the Merrimack Valley, the bus 
company went on strike as of July 1st, leaving us citizens with a big question. How am I 
supposed to get where I need to go? The bus company and the mechanics we know are 
on strike; they are striking for fair wages, and they are striking for Saturday overtime. 
Saturday overtime has been a thing since 1976, and the company has not complied with 
it. As a daily passenger of MEVA, I rely deeply on the service they offer. Every single 
day I take the bus to commute back and forth to UMass Lowell where I study 
mathematics to become a future educator. Without this bus service, many residents like 
me who do not have a car or alternative means of transportation are completely stranded 
and relying on ride shares isn't an option right now. Ubers and Lyfts have become 
incredibly pricey because of the surge in demand caused by the strike. When the buses 
stop running, life doesn't just pause. Simple everyday tasks that keep our lives moving 
forward become major hurdles. It means I can't easily get to places I need to get to, such 
as the Nevins Library to return my library book that is due, or get to other stuff like other 
citizens, such as getting to the post office to take care of important mail. It means people 
can't get access to their work and earn a paycheck or get groceries to feed their families

and that's just a couple of reasons. There are so many more places around Methuen the 
bus goes to, such as the Loop that is serviced by three bus routes that Merrimack Valley 
Transit offers, the Merrimack Plaza serviced by three key routes, the Methuen Square 
which is also serviced by three key routes, and so many other places. People take the bus 
for so many reasons, to hang out with friends, to take it to work and back home. People 
take it to the gym, people take it to go grocery shopping, people take it to go see the 
scenery, people take it to school and university like I do, people take it to doctor and 
medical appointments, and the elderly and retired take it just to go out for the day and 
not be home all day. The bus strike has felt like the COVID-19 pandemic all over again. 
And let me tell you about a couple of residents in Methuen who have been relying on the 
bus. Julie, a resident of Methuen who relies on Meva to go grocery shopping and go out 
to places to the Loop with the bus strike happening, she can't get to these places. She had 
to get her groceries delivered during the strike and paid $11 plus the total on top of what 
her groceries cost. On top of that, she's talking about paying like $11 for a ride share to 
get to the Loop, to get to the train station in Lawrence, Massachusetts, and she's been 
taking the bus since 1996, so for 30 years. And we have Myra who's a resident of Lowell 
but is a worker here in Methuen. Right now, with the strike happening, she can't get 
back and forth to work, so she is missing days of work where she could be making a 
paycheck, but she relies on two buses to get back to Lowell. Some residents complained 
that they had to walk to their job or even call out from work, possibly getting fired from 
their job because of a bus strike. I really hope the bus strike comes to a halt soon because 
so many residents rely on the bus service each and every single day. Thank you.” 
• Tim Vermette, 28 Weybossett Street, Methuen. “I'm here for the Methuen Rail Trail. 
I'm the President. So, I watched the last City Council meeting, and I watched the 
discussion between you guys. So, you're all familiar with why I'm here and kind of what 
I want to do and work with the city. I've talked to a lot of you about it. I've also talked to 
the VFW and the union, the laborer’s union, about this. So, part of the problem that I 
see is that there are questions that are unanswered and it's a loop that goes around and 
around and we never seem to get the actual answer and the problem solved. So, I'd like 
you guys to kind of find a medium ground of can we get the three parties together, the 
city, the union, the VFW together and figure out something one way or the other. It's 
either going to be yes or it's going to be no. So, if it's yes, please get that to that point and 
if it's going to be no, let me know and the rail trail will come up and figure something 
out on our own to possibly take care of those overhangs. We've been looking for funding 
as it is now. There are several different areas where we can get funding to fix that. I was 
talking to John Hadley today. He has an architect friend, and he was going to look at 
seeing if he could have that person come in and give us an estimate as to what it would 
cost to fix it. That way we have a ballpark, and we have a starting point and then from 
there we would look at hiring bodies and a company to do it. So, I don't have anything 
else for you guys. You guys know why I'm here and I appreciate your time. Thank you.” 
• Alejandro Baez, 152 Center Street and member of the Methuen School Committee,

grievance but to show a support for these contracts. We on the School Committee have

• Lieutenant Michael Ferris - Deputy Chief – Motion to appoint by Clr. Simard, 
seconded by Clr. DiZoglio – Discussion – Chair Soto recognized Assistant Fire Chief

written statement, I just wanted to say that both are gentlemen that we're putting before you 
tonight --- I'm sure every one of you know them. They are outstanding candidates. They 
volunteer literally hundreds of hours every year to this city. They cook for the seniors. They 
cook for the veterans. They cook at the Fishing Derby. They do all the shopping. They are 
all volunteering. They're at every city event. Both of these guys are just amazing candidates. 
So back to Lieutenant Ferris. Given the budget challenges we're facing today I'd like to 
emphasize that these promotions are contractual obligations. They're not new positions or 
discretionary promotions. This Deputy Chief position is fully budgeted and full of vacancy 
created by the retirement at the end of June by Deputy Chief Scott Sullivan. It's my pleasure 
to recommend Lieutenant Mike Ferris for promotion to Deputy Chief. Mike is the top 
candidate on the promotional eligibility list. No candidate has been bypassed. Since joining 
the Methuen Fire Department in 2008, Mike has demonstrated exceptional dedication, 
professionalism, and leadership. He served 14 years as a firefighter EMT before being 
promoted to Lieutenant in 2022 where he has successfully led engine and ladder company 
operations, supervised personnel, maintained apparatus readiness, and prioritized firefighter 
safety. Mike is a respected leader and mentor who takes pride in developing younger 
firefighters and fostering a culture of accountability and teamwork. His commitment to 
service extends beyond the firehouse through active participation in community events 
throughout Methuen. He's a familiar presence at city parades and volunteers at all local 
gatherings such as annual Fishing Derby, veterans cookouts, a senior supper, I could go on 
and on. Outside of a service to the community, Mike is a devoted father of his two sons ---

• Firefighter Eric Moreau – Lieutenant - Motion to appoint by Clr. Drew, seconded by 
Clr. Santos – Discussion – Chair Soto recognized Assistant Fire Chief Daniel Donahue, 
“I'm pleased to recommend Firefighter Eric Moreau for promotion to Lieutenant and 
respectfully request your support. This budgeted position fills the vacancy we created by 
Lieutenant Mike Ferris's promotion to Deputy Chief and satisfies the contractual 
apparatus staffing requirements. Eric is the top candidate on the promotional list, and no 
candidates have been bypassed. Since joining the Fire Department in 2015, Eric has 
earned the respect of both members and chief officers through his professionalism, 
leadership and dedication. His leadership skills were forged during his service in the U.S. 
Army where he rose to the rank of Corporal and Squad Leader. His service includes 
deployment in support of Operation Enduring Freedom as well as support for the Boston 
Marathon. Eric is a graduate of the Massachusetts Fire Academy and holds certifications 
as nationally certified EMT, firefighter one and two, fire instructor, along with the 
Associate's Degree in Fire Protection Technology. He is committed to mentoring newer 
members while continuously advancing his own professional development. During 18 
months as an Acting Lieutenant, Eric successfully supervised personnel, managed 
emergency operations, maintained accountability and ensured crew safety. His calm 
demeanor, sound judgment and effective communication consistently demonstrates his 
readiness for permanent promotion. Eric's commitment to the fire service extends 
beyond daily operations. He currently serves as a President of Local 1691, contributes to 
the Honor Guard and the PFF member assistance teams with strong focus on mental 
health. He is very active in the community and not only coaches but serves on the board 
for Methuen Girls Softball League. He's a devoted husband to his high school sweetheart 
of over 20 years, Stephanie, and proud father of their three children, Jaden, 18, Natalia, 
13, Luciana, 11. Eric Moreau possesses the leadership, experience, education and 
character necessary to excel as a lieutenant. I'm confident he will continue to serve the 
citizens of Methuen with integrity and distinction and I strongly recommend him for this 
promotion and thank you for your continued support.” Chair Soto said, “In my 31 
months of service here as a Methuen City Council, I can honestly say that soon-to-be 
Lieutenant Moreau, I believe, has been very impressive on how he advocates for your 
department and I've seen him personally build his relationship with the previous body 
but also with this body. So I am a proud constituent having him serve us here in 
Methuen and I wanted to make sure I voiced that.”  - UPON ROLL CALL VOTE –

time to begin the process of searching for a new VSO, we put together a committee to

community, and he shared what I thought was an outstanding recommendation to bring

there were eight candidates that applied, and everyone brought something to the table,

that facilitated such an opportunity to be able to do so. I was honored to be brought in 
early on and really formulated some of the questions. You know, you could gauge for 
knowledge, you could gauge for experience, but what you really captured was the 
passion. And with Jordan Normandia, I think that you really, Mr. Mayor, got it right. 
Three candidates were selected to be offered to the Mayor as finalists, and when I got the 
call from the Mayor, I knew that the process was followed. Jordan brings a vast 
experience here in Methuen from what I learned in his resume and in interviewing him, 
but what I also learned was the very candidates that came to that table were very 
passionate people who wanted to serve the residents of Methuen and really continue to 
improve upon the services and that every veteran deserves, not only those that are living 
here, but those that will arrive in your community every given year. There will be 
veterans coming in as service members going into the military. Whether they have roots 
in Methuen or they're looking to establish those roots, I think you have a great candidate 
tonight who will continue to serve as many great veteran service officers have done in 
the city. So, I really thank you all for the opportunity, and I wish you all the very best. 
I'm here as a resource, and if I could ever be of some support, please don't hesitate to call 
upon me. Thank you.” Chair Soto recognized Jordan Normandia, “Thank you, Madam

say thank you for the opportunity to speak with you regarding my potential appointment

but as an opportunity to continue serving those who have served our nations and their

military careers. I also served as an instructor for the Department of Defense's Transition

community. Professionally, my municipal career has provided me with extensive

family in Bethune is treated with dignity, respect, and professionalism, and receives
